quote: I looked into the whole thing before, but I didn't like it because of the prices, because of the terms, and a lot of stuff.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a full prior solar shopping experience with a specific complaint (price, terms) and a decision to wait for market maturity/reviews. This is exactly the kind of competitive intelligence a closer would want, and it also directly maps to the objection_inversion trigger for cost.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this as low-value background chatter not worth digging into on a short qualifying call.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask one follow-up — which company, what was the quoted price/terms — even 10-15 seconds of probing gives the closer usable context and might have surfaced the objection_inversion opening ('what's actually expensive is the bill you're still paying').

quote: Yeah. Yeah. Kinda get a little bit more research through. Yeah.
stewart_read: The customer's stated reason for holding off (price/terms too high) is the textbook objection_inversion trigger — the same bill pain that justifies solar is being used as the reason to wait. The rep validates the wait-and-see logic instead of flipping it.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically not pushing because the call was headed toward a credit disqualification anyway and pushing here wouldn't change that outcome.
coaching_implication: This moment happened before the credit qualifier was reached — the rep didn't yet know the call would DQ. The flip should have been tried here regardless of downstream outcome; replay this clip to show the missed reframe opportunity.

quote: I do wanna just make sure that I was taking a look at the the address there. You have a very beautiful home, gets lots and lots of sunlight, so that's great to see.
stewart_read: A small, genuine rapport touch tied to the actual property — a good example of calm, neighbor-like energy rather than a scripted compliment.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this move — it's a low-cost, specific personalization technique worth repeating on other calls.

quote: And then in order to qualify for the current programs going on right now, all we ask of the homeowner is you just have a credit score of at least 670. Is that gonna be an issue for you guys?
stewart_read: Rep runs the credit qualifier as scripted and DQs on the customer's stated answer for both homeowner and spouse. Per the schema's unresolved Kenny policy question, this may be correct procedure (setter DQs on stated) or a lost deal if the intended policy is closer-pull-decides.
alternative_hypothesis: If Ion's actual policy is 'let the closer's credit pull decide,' this DQ is a coaching gap; if setter DQ-on-stated is correct policy, this is compliant execution.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny per qualifiers.credit_qualifier.policy_question_for_kenny — until resolved, don't coach this rep on the DQ decision itself, but note the missing mention of alternative purchase/financing options for sub-670 customers.

stewart_read: Customer doesn't understand what a credit score requirement means in this context, forcing the rep to repeat the line verbatim rather than clarify or simplify.
alternative_hypothesis: This could simply be a hearing/connection issue rather than genuine confusion about the concept of credit score.
coaching_implication: Minor — the rep's repeat was adequate, but a plain-language reframe ('basically your FICO score, the number lenders use') might land faster with less-financially-fluent customers.

quote: I I'll make a note here to follow-up with you in a couple of months just to see where everything's kind of at, but I'll take you off our list for now.
stewart_read: The DQ exit has no specific date, no clear next step, and no handshake — just a vague 'couple months' promise before hanging up.
alternative_hypothesis: Given this is a hard credit DQ (not a booking), a full button-up isn't applicable — but a specific follow-up date (e.g., 'I'll call you back in March') would still make the promise concrete rather than vague.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to give a specific month/date for DQ follow-ups rather than 'a couple months' — makes the promise trackable and more credible to the customer.
